newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher as exporters buy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher as exporters buy.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended higher against its American counterpart on Friday on active U.S. dollar sales by exporters and an influx of foreign equity funds, dealers said.
The Taiwan dollar finished at T$27.435, off an intra-day high of T$27.426, but well above Thursday's T$27.443 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$272 million.

Despite the persistantly strong U.S. dollar overseas, the local currency remained relatively strong as exporters sold the greenback for funds to pay bonuses for their employees ahead of the Chinese new year on February 7, dealers said.
"The strong demand for Taiwan dollars and the influx of foreign equity funds pushed the local unit up," a dealer said, adding this condition would continue for some time before the Chinese new year.
A range of T$27.42-T$27.45 range is seen in future sessions.
